text:
ashwin: Heads up — seeing intermittent packet loss between pods during GPU backfills in us-east-1. Flows to /backfill svc show ~20-30% retransmits for short bursts, not constant.
maria: When did this start?
ashwin: Around 10:40 UTC coincident with a large autoscale (≈200 GPUs added). Problem windows last 2–5 minutes.
devon: Any pattern by node pair or rack?
ashwin: Mostly within the same AZ, across multiple node pairs. I captured a small pcap — tcpdump shows repeated SYN/ACK retransmits and lots of geneve encapsulated fragments. Sample lines:
```
10:42:11.123456 IP 10.0.32.45.58654 > 10.0.48.12.8080: Flags [P.], seq 1:143, ack 1, win 29200, length 142
10:42:11.123789 IP 192.168.1.12.57678 > 192.168.1.34.6081: UDP, length 1620  # geneve outer
10:42:11.223999 IP 10.0.48.12.8080 > 10.0.32.45.58654: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
```
chen: Can you paste `ip -s link` and `ethtool -S` for vxlan/underlay on one of the impacted nodes? Also `ss -s`.
ashwin: Pasting snippets from gpu-az2-17 (impacting):
```
# ip -s link show vxlan0
3: vxlan0: mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default \n    RX: bytes 1251834 packets 10234 errors 0 dropped 18 overruns 0 carrier 0
    TX: bytes 982312 packets 8765 errors 0 dropped 12 overruns 0 carrier 0
# ethtool -S ens4 | grep -E "rx_missed|tx_errors|gso"
rx_missed: 2
tx_errors: 0
gso_segs: 128
# ss -s | grep retrans
retrans: 312 (out of 1400 packets)
```
infra-bot: Alert: OverlayRetransmitRate > 10% in us-east-1 (10:47 UTC) :rotating_light:
devon: Could be offload/GRO/GSO interaction with geneve during node handoff/pod migration. We've hit conntrack + encap offload mismatches before. Also possible path MTU + fragmentation since mtu is 1450.
samir: Also check whether these nodes are on RDMA-enabled hardware — some NIC drivers change offload semantics which can break encapsulated packet handling.
maria: Quick canary: disable GRO/GSO on vxlan0 on one node and rerun the backfill test. Command: `ethtool -K vxlan0 gro off gso off` — do it on a drained canary so we don't drop real traffic.
ashwin: Running that now on gpu-az2-17 and kicking off a short backfill. Collecting `ss -s` and tcpdump. Preliminary `ss` shows retrans down:
```
before: retrans: 312/1400 (~22%)
after: retrans: 16/1340 (~1.2%)
```
devon: Nice. If that holds, we should roll to a small subset of the autoscale pool and monitor. Also consider adjusting sysctl `net.core.rmem_default` and enabling RPS/XPS on the underlay to spread interrupts.
chen: If this is driver offload mismatch, we should: 1) make a k8s DaemonSet to set ethtool flags at boot for GPU image OR 2) add a kernel cmdline/udev rule in our GPU AMI, and 3) file ticket with NIC vendor for firmware/driver behavior on encap.
infra-bot: Deploybot: scheduled canary change (vxlan offload toggles) on node gpu-az2-17 at 11:20 UTC.
ashwin: Canary results look good — retransmits dropped to ~1.2% and application latency normalized. Rolling to 3 more nodes now. Monitoring window 30m. :thumbsup:
samir: Also record node labels (rdma:true/false), driver version, and kernel build in the alert payload so the console can correlate future spikes to those fields.
maria: I'll add an alerting rule to trigger on sudden 5m jumps in overlay retransmit % + include node metadata.
ashwin: Filed INFRA-1423 with pcap, ethtool outputs, and the canary notes. Will update the ticket with roll status after 30m. Thanks folks.
